evals.name: swiftui-navigation-flow
evals.prompt: Add a SwiftUI detail screen from this existing list and verify that back navigation preserves the list state.
expected_behavior: Inspects the existing navigation and state ownership before editing
Uses the project's deployment target and native SwiftUI navigation APIs
Builds and launches with the project's existing Xcode workflow
Uses Agentsims to observe, open a detail, navigate back, and inspect the resulting list state
Does not treat a successful build as runtime proof

evals.name: react-native-shared-form
evals.prompt: Fix this React Native sign-up form so validation and keyboard dismissal work on iOS and Android.
expected_behavior: Preserves the project's form, navigation, and state patterns
Tests asymmetric valid and invalid inputs rather than only app launch
Uses the exact Agentsims device IDs and fresh observations for input targeting
Exercises the changed flow on both iOS and Android when both are available
Reports either cross-platform evidence or the unavailable platform as unverified

evals.name: android-accessibility
evals.prompt: Make this Jetpack Compose icon button accessible and confirm the fix on the running emulator.
expected_behavior: Uses native Compose semantics and follows nearby component patterns
Rebuilds and launches the changed app before device verification
Correlates the Agentsims screenshot with the accessibility element frame
Checks label, role, enabled state, and Android visibility instead of only tapping the button
Refreshes the tree after the fix and observes the resulting screen after interaction

evals.name: no-device-fallback
evals.prompt: Refactor this mobile data service. No simulator or emulator is available in this environment.
expected_behavior: Does not start unrelated device setup for a non-UI refactor
Preserves behavior and follows the project's existing service boundary
Runs focused tests and repository-required checks
Does not claim runtime verification
States only material device behavior that remains unverified

evals.name: react-native-source-inspection
evals.prompt: A React Native checkout button has the wrong accessibility label. Use the running iOS app to find the source and fix it.
expected_behavior: Finds the element from a fresh image and accessibility observation
Inspects the element label, role, value, frame, and test or native identifiers
Uses React Native source confidence and match reason before claiming an exact source location
Does not present a host element owner name as the native node's exact component identity
Rebuilds and confirms the corrected label in a fresh accessibility observation

evals.name: ios-webcam-injection
evals.prompt: Use the available Mac webcam to verify that this iOS camera app renders a live preview in Simulator.
expected_behavior: Builds and launches the camera app before configuring the camera
Uses the public Agentsims camera command and does not inject an arbitrary image or video file
Lists available webcams before selecting one for the intended foreground app
Observes the app and verifies the live preview instead of trusting source-selection success
Stops only task-owned camera injection and notes that stopping the helper can terminate attached apps

evals.name: hardware-volume-buttons
evals.prompt: Verify that this media screen responds correctly to volume-up and volume-down on both available platforms.
expected_behavior: Uses the public press command instead of pixel coordinates
Uses only volume-up and volume-down names supported by both selected platforms
Uses the returned post-action state and observes again when that evidence is not enough
Checks the app's resulting volume state instead of trusting command success
Reports either cross-platform evidence or an unavailable platform as unverified

evals.name: device-condition-recovery
evals.prompt: Confirm that this Android app shows its offline recovery state under a slow disconnected network and returns to normal afterward.
expected_behavior: Checks the selected device's reported network-control capabilities
Records the initial network state and changes conditions through the Agentsims browser
Exercises and observes both the offline state and successful recovery
Does not treat a control toast or lack of a crash as proof
Restores the initial network state after the scenario

evals.name: ios-permission-denial
evals.prompt: Verify that the iOS app explains camera denial and recovers after camera access is allowed.
expected_behavior: Targets the foreground app and records its initial camera permission state
Uses the public Agentsims permissions command with the exact device ID and app bundle ID
Observes the denied state and verifies its accessibility semantics
Allows camera access and verifies the app's recovery path
Restores the initial permission state when the test owns the change

evals.name: observe-payload-handling
evals.prompt: Show me what is currently on screen on the booted device.
expected_behavior: Uses plain observe for readable AX and the saved image path
Reads the saved image with an image tool when visual evidence is needed
Uses the one public view instead of looking for a duplicate raw AX tree
Uses screenshot only when pixels without AX are sufficient
Keeps any ref or capture ID limited to the current device state

evals.name: accessibility-frame-to-coordinate
evals.prompt: Tap the Sign in button on the booted device.
expected_behavior: Observes first and locates the element by a current ref, label, or test ID
Uses the current ref instead of converting the accessibility frame
If AX cannot name the target, uses an image point with the matching current capture ID
Reads dispatch, verification, and the returned post-action state
Reports that the target is absent instead of guessing an unbound coordinate
